You just swallowed your gum, and everyone says it will sit inside you for seven years.
But your gut doesn't work like that.
Gum is mostly a rubbery lump that your body can't digest.
Can't digest isn't the same as can't leave.
Your gut squeezes everything along, one slow wave at a time.
The sweet parts dissolve, and the rubbery lump rides out with the leftovers.
Doctors say that usually takes a few days.
Swallowing lots of gum can, rarely, cause a blockage, so don't make a habit of it.
So your gum isn't staying seven years. It's just taking the long way out.
